title: v1 weekly state machine executions for one week, v2
description: The document at `legacy/weekly/{week_anchor}/executions.json` (crucible.keys.legacy_weekly_executions_key), PRODUCED by nous-ergon-ops/scripts/legacy_weekly_executions_producer.py and CONSUMED by crucible.gate._clause_old_weekly_within_cadence. v1 carried one integer, `executions_started`; Brian's 2026-09-04 ruling (alpha-engine-config-I9756) made the phase-0 metric 'executions that PASSED WeeklyRunDayGate per week', which one integer cannot answer, so v2 files the per-execution facts and the consumer classifies them (alpha-engine-config-I9962). A v1 document is read as UNMEASURABLE, never as a pass. The producer states facts only: no field here says whether an execution passed the gate, because the threshold that decides that is reviewable only beside the clause that applies it.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS schema. A consumer that does not recognise the version refuses the document rather than guessing — which is what makes the key safe to reuse across a schema change.

executions_started.description: Every execution started in the week, regardless of launch source. Retained from v1 for backward reading, and REQUIRED to equal the length of `executions`: a document that answers 'how many' twice with two answers is refused, not reconciled.

executions.description: One entry per execution started in the week, ordered oldest-first so two reads of the same week produce byte-identical documents.

source.description: How the reading was taken, in prose: the API called, how it was paginated, the window, and what the producer did NOT decide.

name.description: The Step Functions execution name. Load-bearing, not decoration: a `watch-rerun-*` name identifies a rerun ISSUER and fails the consuming clause regardless of duration.

stop.description: ISO-8601 `stopDate`, or null for an execution still RUNNING at the moment of the read.

duration_seconds.description: stop - start in seconds, or null when there is no stop. Null is never 0: the consumer treats 'no duration' as 'not a Succeed-skip', and 0 would read as the fastest possible skip — the one value that would exclude a live run from the count grading it.

status.description: The Step Functions execution status verbatim (SUCCEEDED, FAILED, RUNNING, TIMED_OUT, ABORTED). Not normalised: the consumer's Succeed-skip rule is keyed on SUCCEEDED specifically.
